subject.title: macOS XProtect flags bundled @earendil-works/pi-tui darwin-modifiers.node when launching OpenClaw server

question: Should OpenClaw continue distributing `@earendil-works/pi-tui`'s Darwin native modifier helper in server/dashboard installs, and what signing, notarization, replacement, or loading boundary is required?
rationale: The remaining choice affects a bundled native dependency and macOS security tooling; automation can confirm the package/hash but cannot decide the acceptable trust boundary or packaging tradeoff.

options.title: Reproduce and mitigate before stable release
options.body: Run a macOS arm64 packaged install/server launch repro and require either signed/notarized native bits, a dependency replacement, or a packaging split before calling the issue fixed.

options.title: Document as accepted false positive
options.body: Keep the dependency only if maintainers verify the XProtect result is a false positive and publish enough provenance and operator guidance to make that acceptable.

options.title: Remove native helper from non-TUI paths
options.body: Refactor packaging or imports so server/dashboard launches do not ship or load the Darwin modifier helper unless the interactive TUI needs it.

recommendation.title: Reproduce and mitigate before stable release
recommendation.body: Run a macOS arm64 packaged install/server launch repro and require either signed/notarized native bits, a dependency replacement, or a packaging split before calling the issue fixed.

likelyOwner.reason: They recently owned the upstream Pi runtime audit and dependency bump that touched the exact package surface.
